item.title: Top 5 Best Pokémon TCG Cards From Delta Reign
item.description:
Pokémon|competitive

Top 5 Best Pokémon TCG Cards From Delta Reign

Rayquaza is amazing, but have you seen this spicy bird?

By Natalie Millar

|@nataliem9999
|

Published Oct 27, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Hello everyone! Delta Reign is almost here and with the new expansion we have some new cards to talk about! This set does introduce the new split Stadium mechanic which pushes for stronger Stadiums at the cost of having to play both halves of the Stadiums from your hand, and outside of these there are a bunch of strong cards!

The Best Cards From Delta Reign

Honorable Mention

Aarune is a spiritual reprint of Scott from EX Emerald, which saw a bunch of play back in the mid 2000s. Aarune is a very slow card; using your Supporter for turn to only find other Supporters and Stadiums is generally very weak in the Pokémon TCG, but if a deck is intending to be slow then Aarune can be a very strong partner for it. Slower control decks generally rely heavily on Supporter cards for their strongest effects, and since you can find Aarune from another Aarune, the best way to use this card will likely be from chaining them together. Another aspect of Aarune is that you can use it alongside the new split Stadiums, making them significantly easier to put in play. Aarune is very slow and will be unlikely to be played in normal attacking decks, but has potential in slower, more controlling lists.

#5 Tasty Rice Ball

Jumbo Ice Cream has seen a bunch of play in slower control decks such as Crustle and Kangaskhan/Boufallant, and Tasty Rice Ball is a very similar card. The first Tasty Rice Ball only heals 30 from your active Pokémon, but  each subsequent Tasty Rice Ball heals an additional 30, with the final Tasty Rice Ball healing 120 damage. If you use all four Tasty Rice Ball throughout the game you heal 300 damage, and while this is less than the 320 you would heal from Jumbo Ice Creams, you can use Tasty Rice Ball while your active Pokémon has less than three Energy attached. I'm not currently expecting Tasty Rice Ball to surpass Jumbo Ice Cream, but I think it could supplement it for additional healing.

#4 Adventuring Lantern

Earthen Vessel was one of the strongest cards in the format for a long time, and while Adventuring Lantern is not as good as Earthen Vessel was, it's still a very strong card. Many decks want access to Energy, and while you can only use Earthen Vessel for Fire and Lightning Energy, it's still a powerful card. Any deck that uses either type of Energy can likely consider including Adventuring Lantern, as the additional type can be used for Colorless Energy costs. Many decks also use Crispin and can use the additional type to fuel the acceleration effect on Crispin, and I also believe that Adventuring Lantern will be combined with the next card on this list.

#3 Mega Rayquaza ex

Mega Rayquaza ex is the headliner of this set and I think it has a ton of competitive potential. It's a 280 Basic Pokémon, and has the Roar of the Ruler ability that lets you look at the top four cards of your deck and attach a Basic Energy you find there to it, then Storm Emeralda does 50 damage for each Fire and Lightning Energy on your board. You do need to get to six and sometimes seven Energy in play to take big knockouts, but you can use Ethan's Ho-Oh ex's Golden Flame ability to attach extra Energy every turn and fuel Storm Emeralda. Outside of that, you can also use Crispin and multiple Mega Rayquaza, alongside Area Zero Underdepths to fuel Energy in play, and I could see Storm Emeralda quickly ramping to a point where it's taking one-hit knockouts on anything. I would expect this deck to play similarly to the current Basic Box decks, and I imagine they will include the number one card on this list as well!

#2 Legendary Pyroduct

There are a few Legendary Stadiums in this expansion, but I think the strongest one is Legendary Pyroduct. Shutting off the abilities of all evolution Pokémon is very powerful and will likely be a mainstay at some point in its lifetime. Currently, it turns off the Powerful Hand abilities of the Alakazam line, Run Away Draw from Dudunsparce, Drakloak's Recon Directive and Crustle's Mysterious Rock Inn, as well as shutting off a number of other decks in the metagame. The biggest downside of this card is that the two halves of the Stadiums are difficult to piece together, putting a big roadblock in place for playing it early. Given how powerful the effect of this card is, I believe it'll see competitive play even though it's very difficult to put into play.

#1 Talonflame ex

One of the strongest cards in the format currently is Mega Kangaskhan ex. Many decks rely on the Run Errand ability to draw tons of cards, and it also cleanly activates the Exciting Dive ability on this Talonflame ex, allowing you to put it directly into play. It has 280 HP, free retreat and for two Energy it can use Talon Hunt, which does 150 and searches your deck for two cards and adds them to your hand. This is a fantastic card for any big basic deck as it's a very strong two-Prize attacker in the early game. You set up your hand with Talon Hunt, and even facilitate a later Legendary Pyroduct alongside a Judge to disrupt any evolution deck, or just build up an attacker next turn. I would expect Talonflame ex to be slotted into many of the various big basic decks in the format and be used as a strong two-Prize attacker.

item.title: How to Build Zane and Killjoy in Silver Age
item.description:
Flesh and Blood|competitive

How to Build Zane and Killjoy in Silver Age

Interested in building either of the new heroes from Smash Palace: Chorus of Steel? Karol has you covered!

By Karol Ruszkiewicz

|

Published Oct 30, 2026

|

6 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Two brand-new Silver Age-legal heroes join the ranks with Smash Palace: Chorus of Steel: Zane and Killjoy. They're both Warriors... but with a twist! Zane, Broadly Beloved is Revered, while Killjoy, the Crooked Blade is a Reviled Thief.

These combinations introduce entirely new class and talent pairings to the game, opening up fresh avenues for deckbuilding exploration. While there aren't many direct mechanical links between Warrior and the Revered or Reviled talents, both heroes have interesting abilities that give them a unique identity.

Zane, Broadly Beloved

Zane's greatest strength is... well, his strength. He can wield two two-handed swords, which is already an incredible ability for a Warrior. Weapons dictate a Warrior's strategy and deck construction, so choose wisely!

Let's start with the wager payoffs: Celebrant Broadsword, Zane's signature weapon, and Golden Grail. Both offer solid rewards for winning wagers, and giving your weapon go again is a dream for many Warriors. However, this strategy leaves plenty of agency in your opponent's hands.

Similarly, Zane's hero ability is a double-edged sword, no pun intended. Allowing your opponent to choose when you both draw a card can have a huge impact on the game. I'd recommend exploring this strategy against heroes that rarely want to defend. You'll also want to pack plenty of attack reactions to give yourself more control over whether your weapon attacks hit.

Other weapons offer pure efficiency, with Dawnblade and Talishar, the Lost Prince being the two standout options.

At a baseline, Dawnblade offers a three-power attack for one resource, comparable to other dual-wielding setups like double Cintari Sabers or Hatchets of Body and Mind. That comparison alone highlights the sheer power of Zane's ability.

With a single red Run Through and a blue card, you can present attacks for three and then six damage. That's efficiency even Ira would be jealous of!

From there, you can experiment with other ways to grant go again. Lead with Speed, Hit and Run, and other Warrior staples work incredibly well with a dual-Dawnblade setup. Once you start incorporating Flurry generators like Edict of Steel, or Take the Lead to generate Blade Dance tokens, the possibilities really open up.

Talishar, the Lost Prince offers an alternative against decks looking to end the game quickly. Playing against a Wizard or an aggressive Ninja? Maybe that extra damage is exactly what you need to close things out.

It does come at an additional resource cost, so you'll probably need to adjust your cost curve, but experimenting with different configurations, such as Dawnblade and Talishar or a wager sword alongside Dawnblade, opens up some fascinating deckbuilding possibilities.

Cheers!

What about the Revered side of things?

If stacking Toughness tokens is your thing, you could cosplay as Tuffnut with four intellect and two enormous swords.

Cards like Dig In and Humble Entrance can help fuel powerful, disruptive defensive cards like Disarm and Disperse. They might be a little tricky to line up, but they're interesting options to consider when building your resource base.

The really exciting part of the Revered card pool is the selection of cards that cheer you.

While winning wagers can generate cheers fairly reliably, the ideal time to make both players draw cards is at the very end of your opponent's turn, preferably when they're out of action points and already have a card ready for arsenal.

That's why cards like Helm of the Adored, Shining Courage, and Will of the Crowd offer some of the most compelling cheer synergies.

Aggro or Control?

So how does Zane actually play? Does he lean into aggressive damage output or take a more controlling approach with Toughness tokens?

The beauty of having such a wide card pool is that you can adjust that balance however you like.

Cards like Hit and Run let you build wider combat chains, potentially even making attack-chain finishers viable. Other cards like Snatch, Flock of the Feather Walkers, and Smash Up could also work alongside your weapon attacks.

I'm incredibly curious to see how players approach Zane. He offers something genuinely new to the Warrior class, and I suspect there's plenty of room for experimentation.

Killjoy, the Crooked Blade

Killjoy shines in Ultimate Pit Fight, but when it comes to Silver Age her hero ability and weapon are much more dependent on the metagame–particularly when it comes to stealing Gold. While I expect this hero to excite deckbuilders everywhere, I think her biggest appeal lies in her unique class and talent combination.

Higher Life or Lower Life?

Killjoy's hero ability encourages you to gradually control the game while staying at a lower life total and booing your opponent. However, a decent portion of the Reviled card pool rewards you for having more life than your opponent. Cards like Mocking Blow and Insult to Injury are powerful, but their incentives can clash with Killjoy's ability.

I'd recommend deciding which Reviled synergies you want to prioritize before diving too deeply into deck construction. Trying to maximize both approaches could leave your deck pulling in opposite directions.

Boo!

While getting full value out of Mocking Blow is satisfying, there's something inherently entertaining about making your opponent lose life just because you can. Cards like Horns of the Despised, Villainous Pose, and Concealed Object lean into that fantasy perfectly.

Warrior's Prowess

I could go on and on about the efficiency of cards like Decimator Great Axe, Steel to the Dome and Engage Steel, but the card that really captures the killjoy aspect of this hero is Steelblade Shunt.

Combined with Killjoy's hero ability, Steelblade Shunt opens up an interesting path toward controlling the game and manipulating both heroes' life totals. Playing defensively also gives you more opportunities to trigger her ability, making this a particularly appealing direction for players who enjoy a slower, more reactive style of Warrior.

She's a Thief!

The Thief card pool is still relatively small... for now. But it already offers some incredible counterplay against Gold-based heroes.

If heroes like Olympia, Gravy Bones, and Victor Goldmane start climbing toward the top of the metagame, cards like Light Fingers and Cutpurse Rapier become much more appealing.

And then there's Money or Your Life? That's another fun way to deal some non-physical damage!

Closing Thoughts

If you're an avid brewer like me, you'll already see the world of possibilities these heroes offer. It's not just the combination of Warrior with the Revered and Reviled talents, with a sprinkle of Thief thrown in, but the hero abilities themselves that make Zane and Killjoy so exciting to explore.

They bring something fresh to Silver Age, but if you've never tried multiplayer Flesh and Blood, Smash Palace Warrior is also a great place to start. Not only do you get two fascinating new heroes, but you also get a box full of fun for four players, thanks to the tailor-made event deck.

Whether you're looking to experiment with unconventional Warrior builds or just cause a little chaos around the table, there's plenty to get excited about!

item.title: The Best-Selling Cards from Hyperia City
item.description:
Disney Lorcana|finance

The Best-Selling Cards from Hyperia City

Who is really the Best in Town?

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Oct 30, 2026

|

7 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Hyperia City is proving to be aptly named straight out of the gate. It's all hype in the world of Disney Lorcana off the back of the game's latest booster release. It's just taking a slightly different form than you may expect. 

The set feels like a building block. Between ink drops and some of the new signpost legendries, it's clear that Hyperia City is supposed to be a foundational set for a post-rotation format more than an immediate reshuffle at the current power level. That hasn't prevented certain cards from sneaking into the spotlight already though, and I have a gut feeling that a few hidden gems remain undiscovered or deliberately hidden for events like DLC London. 

Even if I'm incorrect on that front, I think this is a good thing. While I wouldn't have minded a shake-up at the tournament tables right now, my priority is the future of Disney Lorcana. Hyperia City is doing a wonderful job at building my confidence for that next era and that has me feeling pretty wonderful. 

That said, we've learned some lessons about preparing for the future in a TCG over the last couple of years. It pays to be ahead of the curve, snapping up playable cards before they dominate or securing those collectables before they skyrocket in price. This lesson has been woven into the foundations of the Disney Lorcana community since the game received an uptick of attention alongside Wilds Unknown. 

It's an easy enough concept to understand. You don't want to be the last person in the know with these things. 

That's why I'm so keen to watch the data from the first few weeks of Hyperia City like a hawk. There's so much future bottled up in this product that I cannot shake the need to get in on day zero. So, what have all of you eager beavers been buying? Which cards are stealing all your attention? 

#10 Toulouse - Rough and Tumble

Well, that one makes sense. Toulouse is like really good. 

This is more about the past than the future. Toulouse is emblematic of Pete - Games Referee: a character that defined Core Constructed during its tenure. 

Toulouse is notably worse than Pete due to its meagre stat line. A large part of Pete's power was in providing a card that was never blank, and Toulouse won't feel like that. 

That said, a card doesn't need to be as strong as Pete to make the cut. Songs like Circle of Life defining the tournament tables right now, this effect is much needed — especially on a cheap character that you can sneak into play alongside something else. 

#9 Nick Wilde - Toy Drive Officer

I think Nick Wilde - Toy Drive Officer caught a lot of folks off-guard. I've learnt my lesson thanks to Elinor - Renowned Diplomat: do not ignore four-cost characters that can theoretically draw you cards. 

At the moment, the card is only finding a home in a handful of Sapphire Amber Detective-based decks, but this is a great payoff for caring about those synergies! As more Detectives appear, I'm expecting Nick to play a big part in the success of the deck. 

#8 Aurora - Delightful Musician

In contrast, players were expecting big things from Aurora - Delightful Musician immediately after release... and they haven't really materialized yet? 

She's seen periodic play in various Amber Steel and Amber Emerald decks, but nothing is looking particularly cohesive. Aurora is such a dedicated song payoff that I expect her to blossom once there's more songs you're actively happy to play. 

As I said, a building block for the future. That's not a bad thing. 

#7 Cinderella - Unintentional Icon

Cinderella falls somewhere in the middle of expectations. I think most players expected the card to be playable off the back of a premium shift target, but it has proven to be much better than that. 

Cinderella - Dream Come True is a large part of Cinderella - Unintentional Icon's playability no doubt, but the card filtration and additional ink acceleration have proven to be important in their own right. 

If decks like our recently featured Amber Sapphire Princesses brew continue to find their footing, the Unintentional Icon has a bright future.

#6 Shere Khan - Khan Industries CEO

Maybe I was a little foolish to expect the CEO to be at the top, but Shere Khan is currently stuck in middle management instead. This card was almost universally agreed upon as the hottest ticket in Hyperia City prior to release, so it was always going to be difficult to meet those lofty expectations. 

That doesn't mean you should be looking at Shere Khan - Khan Industries CEO as a failure, though. The card is a powerhouse in current Amethyst Steel variants, which are sitting just below the top dogs of the metagame. This card is absurdly powerful in a vacuum, and there will come a metagame where you'll want to own your copies. 

#5 Mulan - Martial Arts Master

Mulan - Martial Arts Master is nuts. It's already proven to be a phenomenal upgrade to Ruby Amethyst midrange, and it will be a big player in any future grindy Ruby strategies. 

It's so rare for an inkable card to be impactful on-play and on-quest, but Mulan will turbocharge your challengers, generate card advantage and allow any five-cost character to swoop in and clean house. The card just does it all and I'm a huge fan of that, because Ruby feels like it has been struggling for a while now. 

The Enchanted variant feels criminally underpriced at $120 dollars frankly. Into my cart they go.

#4 Max Goof - Karaoke Star

As our beloved Senior Content Manager Jason Grabher-Meyer pointed out last week, Max Goof - Karaoke Star was stealing the stage immediately after his reveal. Jason even called it the "Marquee legendary of Hyperia City" — quite a lofty claim if I do say so myself. 

Max Goof breathes new life into his Fabled counterpart Max Goof - Chart Topper, who can immediately rebuy the song you ditch to Sweet Remix on the following turn. Both cards continue to be on the up-and-up when it comes to demand and price point, and I don't see that slowing down until the duo falls out of favor. 

#3 Flash - Efficient Clerk

If I had a nickel for every steel Epic in Hyperia City that looked to redefine how we play the game, I'd have two nickels... which isn't a lot, but it's strange that it happened twice. 

Flash - Efficient Clerk ticks all the boxes. Great stats, difficult to remove and a safety valve to a popular and potent keyword. Mulan hasn't even gotten off the ground yet and Flash has something to say about it! Worried about Madam Mim - Fox in Infinity? Not anymore! 

The existence of Flash changes how decks will be built throughout the future of Disney Lorcana. It's hard to understate that level of impact.

#2 Don Karnage - Debonair Pirate

Word got around reaaaaal fast about the Donfather. This is a Tinker Bell - Giant Fairy for the modern age. Resist? What Resist? There's no resisting when it comes to the Don. 

Much like his inspirational card, Don Karnage - Debonair Pirate is a defendable turn six play that shatters spines when shifted into play on turn four. This card is already blossoming despite the lack of good Shift targets, and I expect it'll only get better once one appears. 

Much like Flash, Don Karnage needs to be on the mind during your deckbuilding. There's an aura that comes with that. 

#1 Mickey Mouse - Best in Town

But if we're talking about a game-defining card, there really was only one option that could sit as the Best in Town. Mickey Mouse is a monster, and you'll need to be prepared for it. 

Inkable in the late game? Check. A kick in the face to remove? Bingo. Ink drops to rush out small characters or accelerate into horrifically big characters? You're starting to get the picture. At no stage of the game (nor frankly in many decks) is Mickey Mouse - Best in Town a bad card. You'll rarely be upset to see it, and it'll steal games when played early all by itself. 

To me, there's no question that it's the most impactful card in Hyperia City. Clearly, the market agrees. I'm just left wondering if the iconic variant will reach the eye-watering price tag of his Fabled counterpart once the set finally goes out of print.

item.title: Create an Artifact Army With Vraska, Soul of Stone in Commander
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|Commander|casual

Create an Artifact Army With Vraska, Soul of Stone in Commander

Leave no stone unturned.

By Cas Hinds

|

Published Oct 31, 2026

|

6 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Commander Bestiary

I've been looking forward to talking about the Reality Fracture version of Vraska for a while now. In this edition of Commander Bestiary, we're talking about what the world would be like if our favorite Gorgon was a Wizard instead of an Assassin. It's a deck that focuses on small noncreature spells, Treasure synergy, and incremental damage. 

Vraska the Unguilded

Vraska is covered in green scales with long black hair in the shape of snakes. She has these bright yellow eyes that shine bright and golden when she uses her powers to turn others into stone. This power will be relevant when discussing her Echoverse version later on.

Vraska hated the institution of power, the Azorius Senate, when she was a child and resented them for pushing Golgari out of certain areas they had dominion over. She was tortured and held captive by the Azorius Senate during their purge. She had to listen to her fellow Golgari being blinded and killed when she was only seventeen. 

When she tried to participate in a rebellion and escape, she was instead recaptured, beaten, and left for dead. Her planeswalker spark ignited and she found herself on another plane with all her ribs broken. Much later, she became the leader of the Ochran, or a secret Golgari cult operating out of the undercity. It was made up of mercenaries who partook in vengeance killings for a price. Nicol Bolas eventually offered her the guildmaster position of the Golgari if she delivered items from Orazca to his agents.

In her journey for Bolas she ended up falling in love with Jace Beleren who was also on Orazca, but in an attempt to keep her love from Nicol Bolas she asked Jace to seal her love away in her mind. She was able to fool Nicol Bolas; kill Jarad, the Golgari Guildmaster; and assume her role as Guildmaster of the Golgari.

Fast forwarding, Vraska joins the gatewatch to stop Elesh Norn. Vraska is caught and forced to fight in Sheoldred's Coliseum. When the gatewatch recovered her, she was already infected with phyresis. Jace stayed with her to play her favorite memories in her mind as she turned, but soon she infected him with phyresis. She becomes fully compleated, body changed, metallic markings all over her, hair turned to cables, and her fingers like claws.

After the events of Elesh Norn's evasion, she is cured of her phyresis alongside Jace. That brings us to the current timeline where she uncovers Loot with Jace, and unwillingly brings about Jace's plan to rewrite the multiverse.The Vraska we'll cover in this article is the Echoverse version of herself, who never had her ability to petrify, if she was never seen as deadly, never had to be.

Slinging The Table With Noncreature Spells

With Vraska as a commander, casting a noncreature spell creates a 1/1 colorless Sculpture Treasure Artifact Creature token. That's a lot of words for a token type, but we'll want to guarantee that we can string together a bunch of noncreature spells to increase the amount of tokens we can make.

We're running a lot of low cost noncreature spells like Flow State, Faithless Looting, and Flashback for card draw and spellslinger fuel that trigger our commander. We're running Unwind and Snap for interaction that keeps mana open. Idol of Oblivion, Skullclamp, and Caretaker's Talent are all good sources of card draw that synergize with the deck making tokens.

Treasure Synergies and Doubling Tokens

One of the essential ways we'll abuse this deck is to cram a few Treasure synergies into it. We're running Xorn to make double the tokens with Vraska's trigger. We're playing Academy Manufactor to potentially triple our token production, making a food and clue version of our creatures. Goldspan Dragon will make our sculptures tap for double mana.

We want to take advantage of artifacts entering the battlefield for damage like Weftstalker Ardent, Reckless Fireweaver, and Ingenious Artillerist. This will be a prominent way we'll deal damage in this deck. It doesn't hurt to throw Purphoros, God of the Forge, Warleader's Call, and Impact Tremors into the mix too. Over the course of the game, the damage can add up. If we can spell sling things enough, maybe a ping damage burn turn will get us to where we need to go.

We're running a bunch of ways to double the amount of tokens we make. We're running Mondrak, Glory Dominus, Elspeth, Storm Slayer, and Anointed Procession. We want to be able to double up on the tokens, double dipping a spell into more mana. Token creation to mana to card ratio is really important,and doubling token production is one way to swing the math well in our favor.

Veyran, Voice of Duality, Harmonic Prodigy, and Wizard's Staff are additional ways to double the commander's trigger, making double the tokens. With something like Mechanized Production, we can cast a noncreature spell on someone's end step, making two tokens, getting us to the eight necessary to win. We won't be able to tap our creature treasures for mana the turn they come in with Vraska's ability because of summoning sickness. If we want to storm off with all the mana we're getting refunded with each noncreature spell, we have to find a way to give our creatures haste.

Roar of Resistance is a low cost, noncreature way to give haste and even make our creatures a little more intimidating as attackers. Samut, Hazoret's Champion can give haste as well. Lightning Greaves is a low cost concreature spell that gives shroud and haste. Frostcliff Siege has the ability to give trample and haste as well.

How Vraska Can Petrify in the Echoverse

You have to get Vraska out as soon as possible if you want to deal a decent amount of damage with this deck. I think the fastest you can do that is turn three, and then you have to get a haste enabler out. We also want to generate more mana to do more on each of our turns. I think Roar of Resistance is ideal here because it will give haste and create a Sculpture token.

Then we're going to put out mana artifacts that trigger Vraska's ability. A Talisman here and there will ramp up the amount of mana we have access to and make more Sculpture tokens. Then we have to get a draw engine into play. We want to be able to keep refueling. Low cost spells usually result in a dead hand. An Idol of Oblivion or a Caretaker's Talent might do nicely here. Maybe even a Kindred Discovery if we want to spring the mana for it. Then we'll want to put out a Xorn, Veyran, or Anointed Procession to speed up our token production process. That alongside an Impact Tremors will start to get life totals nice and low.

Once we've built up enough creatures and have an excess of mana we have a couple of ways to close out the game. We can slam a Banner of Kinship or Shared Animosity to go in with a tall and wide board to close out the game through combat damage. Craterclaw Colossus would be excellent here too because each of the creatures are artifacts. On the other hand, we can also dump all of our mana into a Crackle With Power or a Jaya's Immolating Inferno to close out the game. It's sort of like picking your poison.

item.title: The Top 10 Cards Everybody Wants from GD06 Stardust Trails
item.description:
Gundam Card Game|finance

The Top 10 Cards Everybody Wants from GD06 Stardust Trails

A Level 9 you can play as early as turn 4? Sign me up for that.

By Wren Melburn

|

Published Nov 2, 2026

|

9 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: The Cards Everybody Wants

Now this is something you've been waiting for: the latest set that's generating a ton of hype in the Gundam community is right around the corner. Now we all get to sink our teeth into the new cards!

Dropping into local game stores on October 30th is Stardust Trails, and it's a helluava trail that Bandai has laid for us. But let's get into some of the crazy toys you can open up at your release events:

#10 ZZ Gundam

This card truly should be higher on the list but I just can't wait to talk about a big beefy king of ping. This massive double zeta Unit is crashing down to make a statement, and that statement is that AEUG is not here to play around.

Piloted by Judau Ashta with a killer statline, the ZZ Gundam has a a wicked way to get it into play early with the Core Fighter Gundam Team combo. The ability to slap down multiple little units, and combine them into a Voltron-esqe boss monster ahead of the competition is something that you'll love. Go double zeta go!

ZZ Gundam hits everything for three damage thanks to a combination of its deploy and passive abilities. It's a mean customer. Move out of the way Wing Gundam Zero, there's a new toy to play with.

#9 Shadow Gundam

The Shadow Gundam is great new tech for the Gundam Mobile Fighter fans out there like myself. Interestingly, it's a Unit that can be linked with any of the Gundam Fighter Pilots. This is a great top end for the deck as Master Gundam has been running into a wall due to Argama's huge popularity. So, swap out a few copies of Shining Gundam (Super Mode) or maybe drop a Master Gundam to give it a try!

Not only is a slam dunk of a card that any MF player will want to tinker with, the alt art oozes style, flipping through an attack and caught in an action still. I know for me it's one of the things I want most from the set, and you're not even close to being through this list!

#8 Gundam GP01Fb

Making its series debut, the GP01Fb–now that's a mouthful–from Stardust Memory crosses the skies above you today. The GP01Fb is well positioned as an early game tool to pop shields and dodge blockers with High-Maneuver. Whatever you're throwing it at can't avoid the hit, so that's a massive upside at a time when blocker decks that have been running the format since Strike Freedom hit the scene.

I'm a big fan of Kou Uraki taking advantage of the Unit he links with, because when someone inevitably attacks back into the rested GP01, you'll draw a card, then heal two HP during the Action Phase. Keep in mind y'all that action comes before combat damage, so you can't be sneaky and heal damage before it is dealt.

But hey, card draw and HP recovery? That's some serious stuff that can't be ignored, and that's before you even touch on the High-Maneuver. This is a perfect early-mid game unit that I can see doing a lot, so keep an eye on it during the release season. I know I am! 

#7 Zeta Gundam

It's no surprise to anyone, but the other little Zeta landing on the list is a no-brainer. This thing is nasty, and fits into the game plan of the big AEUG deck by dealing damage and providing you another great link target.

There's not a whole lot to say about a perfect accompaniment to a deck that is getting a bunch of love. So you'll be happy to see it, even if it's just a regular rare. This feels like a Darkness Finger situation. As the deck gets better, these will slowly pop up in the background.

#6 GFreD

The GQuuuuuuX series is back with a vengeance as Nyaan drives the new Alphacide GFred into the game. This one's a much more supportive version than the ping engine before it. There aren't many Alphacide cards yet, but I'm very curious to see how many Bandai will give all of us later, especially with how much love the Clan tag was getting. Besides, the GFeD looks awesome!

But where are you going to use it? The deck I've been seeing online is a Blue/Purple Alphacide one that focuses on bringing back the small Level 3 GQuuuuuuX that gains Blocker, as well as the Level 5 version to throw off your opponent's tempo. On the other side of the deck you'll have the GQuuuuuuX new blue toy to fuel your hand and swing away with a big beefy beater.

This feels like one of those cards that the longer it goes unseen, the better it gets in the background. I know I'm going to personally give it a try when the set drops!

#5 Legend Gundam

ALLLLLLRIGHTYY, ZAFT is back in style and in all caps. This is great for me: I'm just finishing up a rewatch of Gundam Seed Destiny, so seeing the Legend on a card feels great. If you were a massive fan of the ZAFT plan with Destiny and big swings, then Bandai is feeding you real good! 

The Legend is here and it lives up to the name for sure. You'll find the Legend hanging out in an interesting place alongside Minerva Squad: in the trash. I don't mean that in a bad way, but trash shenanigans are just the way that the crew of the Minerva normally roll.

If you look all over the previous Minerva Squad cards you've got here, you can see the pattern emerging. Throw units at opponents with wild abandon and then rip them out of the yard for cheaper with the new Legend or ramp up into the GD04 Destiny. Rey Za Burrel sitting in the pilot seat is cool but not essential as it's the lower cost that you want, but hey I'll always take a damage reduction for clearing out smaller troublesome units.

#4 Gundam Bael

BAEEEEEEEEL, okay I had to do that as someone who played Elden Ring. Moving on to the actual card, it's a sweet Gjallarhorn Unit from IBO that's doing something funky you haven't seen: being GOOD. All jokes aside, the Bael is a beast of a suit that adds some backup to your Red/Purple IBO decks by letting you sneak things in that are Level 6 or less as long as you already have four Gjallarhorn cards in the bin.

Bael's LR++ makes an impact! Showing off a brilliant golden blade and silhouetting McGillis in the background is just sublime. As usual, Bandai gave us some beautiful crispy white and gold detailing for the art, and that just fits perfect for the Bael

#3 Akatsuki (Shiranui)

The man who can make the impossible possible is back again, but hey this Akatsuki can link with any Orb Pilot, so who even needs Mu to start committing war crimes this time around? I know I don't (that's a lie, I still love Mr. La Flaga). But what's the Akatsuki (Shiranui) doing here this time? How do you abuse it?

Well it fits directly into the Blue/White or rather Blue/anything archetype that loves a top end Strike Freedom. Turns out that getting more tools in the Orb box is never a bad plan, and this time it's a repeatable bounce effect to throw off your opponent's tempo. Every attack with the Akatsuki lets you throw something your opponent controls back into hand, and that's nasty. I can only imagine how this is going to feel with the Aile Strike, Sword Strike and this in the same deck, completely throwing off the entire tempo of a game.

I'm not done yet with Orb but I have to move on for just a few moments to another fan favourite, so forgive me for deviating, but if you're a fan of Wing let's flip to the next card, which just feels downright mean.

#2 Altron Gundam (EW)

Moving up to the penultimate spot in the coolest cards of GD06, Wing fans rejoice as the new Altron Gundam makes itself known. Man, Bandai is really letting some of the secondary characters get some love this time around for the set, and I'm here for it. Plus there's a fantastic new Chang Wufei to go with Altron.

I'll be straight up, this is something I'm looking forward to having in my back pocket. The Altron can go toe to toe with the Strike Freedom, and that's something that can't be ignored at all. Plus it's not a super heavy investment, and it only gets better when your opponent has a Level 5 Unit in play. But then again, that's how it tangles with the Strike Freedom.

With Chang in the pilot seat, the Altron is sitting pretty at a 5/5 and that's before you do the opposing Unit buff to raise it to an 8/5. Not only that, but on attack with Chang in the cockpit, you drop an opposing unit by 3 AP when you swing in. So you can safely nail down nasty threats and do it all for the low cost of being on Level 4. Not so shabby at all.

On top of all that, if you're a fan of Wing, you'll be after the stellar alt art that Bandai gave us this time around. The crisp detailing of the light outlining the Altron, juxtaposed against Chang standing in the foreground is just something you need to bling out a deck with. It's going to feel so good to slam on the table, and see your opponent check out the treasure you're rocking.

#1 Infinite Justice Gundam

Topping out the coolest cards from Stardust Trails has to be the Infinite Justice, and oh boy can I see infinite uses for this little number. You'll mostly see it in Orb lists that just need another payoff before they hit the Strike Freedom. Turns out that adding more redundancy to that shell makes for a nasty nasty list. I always found that the turn before you drop SF is where the list makes or breaks it, so having a great option there? Perfect!

It's not bottom decking an opponent's unit, but that on deploy to throw tempo off yet again is something that you can't ignore. My favourite thing is that it hits active units rather than spent, so it removes a Blocker from the board during those really grindy matchups, and that's without having to have the Athrun Zala Link.

Not only does it do the disruption thing, you also get to recover HP when you destroy an enemy card once per turn, for one of your Orb units. Meaning that the Justice can stick around to heal up a SF that goes in hard and comes out with a few scratches, or heal itself. Not so shabby at all.

It wouldn't be the finale of our list without showing off the super duper cool LR++ that Bandai gave us, with the Infinite Justice twirling its dual ended beamsaber. It's no secret that I love Seed, so seeing one of my favourite Mobile Suits get the LR++ treatment just feels awesome! It's something I'm going to be hoping to see during the release event so I can stick it next to the High Grade I have in my office.

item.title: This Month in Japanese Yu-Gi-Oh (October 2026)
item.description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!

This Month in Japanese Yu-Gi-Oh (October 2026)

An Immortal Phoenix rises in Japan along with plenty of other goodies.

By Samuel Frew

|

Published Nov 2, 2026

|

7 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Kia ora koutou! October was another important month for the Yu-Gi-Oh! Official Card Game in Japan, although most of their releases have only just hit the shelves! 

The newest core booster, Immortal Phoenix, has just released for Japanese players, but the three Original Artwork Duel Sets have also been distributed, containing re-releases of the original OCG Structure Decks with classic-style cards and manga-style cards. Of course, there were also the customary VJump promotional cards and the latest episode of the lore anime Yu-Gi-Oh! CARD GAME THE CHRONICLES.

This Month in Japanese Yu-Gi-Oh

The Phoenix is Rising

Immortal Phoenix is the third of Series 14 of the Yu-Gi-Oh! OCG's core boosters, and it's extremely similar to its two predecessors regarding the themes it contains and their distribution within the set.

The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness (extended art)

Yami Marik and the new extended art The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness grace the cover of each Immortal Phoenix pack, and the set contains the new Sun God theme, revamps of many of Yami Marik's most devious torture cards with effective consistency effects and a shared effect to add themselves to your hand if you sent their new Spell The Immortal Sun God to the graveyard that turn.

The Immortal Sun God allows you to revive a Winged Dragon of Ra monster and if you revive The Winged Dragon of Ra itself, you'll be able to send it back to the graveyard to summon The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness. This is the biggest difference between previous Series 14 cover themes, which could be built solely using cards from that set; the Sun God theme requires the original Ra to function. 

All the previous forms of Ra are reprinted in the Immortal Phoenix +1 Expansion Pack, which are included in first print runs of Immortal Phoenix boxes, and The Winged Dragon of Ra - Immortal Phoenix has a new artwork. The pack also includes the extended art IMMORTAL PHOENIX Token.

Amazoness Harpie

Mai Valentine's Battle City deck received a complete revamp, which was hinted at by Harpie Lady - Elegant Egotist in the Original Artwork Collection. These new Amazoness and Harpie cards meld both themes into a Fusion strategy (something long overdue for Harpies) based around monsters that mention Harpie Lady, with varied and potent off-turn disruption effects.

Triangle Ecstasy Harpie Lady Sisters

Amazoness Swordsmaster fits well in existing Amazoness decks, with its extension effect and Quick effect to sacrifice a monster to negate the effects of an opponent's monster and reduce its ATK, while Triangle Ecstasy Harpie Lady Sisters gets really big really quickly, can't be targeted by the effects of non-WIND monsters, and can dust the field of all your opponent's Spells and Traps, can both Fusions can be summoned with each fusing effect in the deck.

Diabellze of the Winter Raven

The tie-in theme for Yu-Gi-Oh! CARD GAME THE CHRONICLES in Immortal Phoenix is the Winter Raven theme, a Sinful Spoils-related theme revolving around Diabellstar's sister Diabellze. This Synchro theme manipulates monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone and aims to summon their ace Fusion Monster, the extended art Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest.

Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest (extended art)

Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest also manipulates your monsters into Continuous Spells, then bounces cards off the field (and that's any cards from any side of the field) equal to the number of Spells and Traps you control, clearing the way for an attack boosted by your Spells and Traps. 

Once Upon a Time, Javelin Beetle Was Anti-Dragon

Immortal Phoenix introduces a big new Ritual theme, the Reindsurm, an Insect Ritual theme composed entirely of Ritual Monsters and Spells (and one Trap). These Ritual Monsters pack anti-Dragon effects that bolster their own considerable resource-gathering, as a reference to Javelin Beetle in Yu-Gi-Oh! The Duelists of the Roses gaining ATK when it battled a Dragon (Javelin Beetle is also retrained here as Javelin Beetle of the Alliance).

Reindsurm Giriakarma

While all the Reindsurm Ritual Monsters can be Ritual Summoned with Reindsurm Conquest, the Level 4 Reindsurm Rituals also have effects that Ritual Summon other Insect Rituals when sent to the graveyard; to compensate for this massive drain on resources, most Reindsurm effects move two cards instead of one.

Smaller Themes

King of Beasts, Risen From the Valley of Flames (extended art)

Salamangreats get five new cards with the aim of boosted their Spell and Trap consistency and introducing the anime card Salamangreat Shrine to prevent your opponent's FIRE monsters from affecting yours, while the reimaged Salamangreat Heatleo, King of Beasts, Risen From the Valley of Flames turns your opponent's monsters into FIRE monsters and combines the effects of the original Heatleo into a potent Quick Effect.

The Ars Magna theme from Beyond the Brave has also been bolstered with a bunch of new Link Monsters that belong to the other Medius lore themes, like Artmage, DoomZ and Elfnote, which can be instantly summoned with their new Field Spell, Ars Magna Academic Arcane Apparition Acropolis.

Rikka also got five new cards, including two strong new Xyz Monsters. Teardrop the Rikka Empress can bypass many protective effects by sending Spells and Traps to the graveyard and Tributing a monster and refresh its materials with cards from your opponent's graveyard every time a monster is Tributed.

Free Agents

Power of the Duelist (extended art)

Immortal Phoenix is the first Series 14 core booster that doesn't have a free agent monster with an extended art. Instead, Power of the Duelist (which also ties in with the currently airing Yu-Gi-Oh! GX remaster) allows you to pull off various effects based on the number of different Attributes among the effects of the monsters your activated that turn.

Lethargisaurus is a different Synchro take on Number 41: Bagooska the Terribly Tired Tapir, which changes every monster on the field to Defense Position and prevents players from chaining to their own cards. It goes so far as to require monsters in Defense Position as its materials. 

With Mind Scan on the horizon in Magnificent Maestros, a card to counter it and similar effects was arguably inevitable. The Secret Crane Princess Who Returns A Favor can punish your opponent for revealing it or reveal herself by bouncing herself back to the hand, destroying all cards they control, and even place itself on top of your deck at the end of their turn.

Original Artwork Duel Sets

The three Original Artwork Duel Sets were shipped to fans who had pre-ordered them earlier in the year. These sets are a nostalgia powerhouse, containing the original Structure Decks Yugi, Kaiba and Joey (the Japanese versions) with the exact same contents in a classic style and manga-style cards. 

In addition, they also come with 100 sleeves, a dice, coin, card case and Duel Field. These products aren't about modern reprints at all, they're full nostalgia, but very cool nostalgia. The Kaiba Duel Set also includes Blue-Eyes White Dragons in Chinese and English, not just Japanese.

Counter Spell?!

The latest "Spell Card"-esque revamp of an old card is the next VJump promotional card, Counter Spell "Negate Attack", which more accurately captures the original Negate Attack from the manga, and adds in references to its effects being used before Kaiba summoned Obelisk the Tormentor.

While not a promotional card, the latest Tournament Pack has also released its newest Normal Monster, The Dark Dragon Lord of Ultum, a Level 8 EARTH Dragon with 2000 ATK and DEF, stats that are likely to come in handy at some point somewhere.

Yu-Gi-Oh! CARD GAME THE CHRONICLES

This month's episode of Yu-Gi-Oh! CARD GAME THE CHRONICLES continued the Sinful Spoils arc and focused on the backstory of Diabellstar the Black Witch and Diabellze the Original Sinkeeper, covering the tragic events in the White Forest. While this episode lacks the awesome action the previous two had, the depiction of Elsette and Astellar's childhood friendship and the corruption of the White Forest are very heartfelt, although it does raise the question of how much the final Sinful Spoils episode will be able to cover.

October was the start of the next big period of releases for Yu-Gi-Oh! in Japan, and the second Revolution Booster coming in November is likely to have an impact as well (although hopefully not as drastically as the previous one). While the 30th anniversary of Yu-Gi-Oh! has passed, the celebrations in the card game are still ongoing!

item.title: Collectibility that's out of this world.Collector's Guide to Star Trekby Emma Merriam-PartlowRead More
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|collecting|finance

Collector's Guide to Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek

Collectibility that's out of this world.

By Emma Merriam-Partlow

|

Published Oct 29, 2026

|

11 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Star Trek is almost here, and with it comes a completely new way to explore Magic: The Gathering. While Star Trek isn't the intellectual property for everyone, it's one with a rich history and dedicated fanbase who'll want nothing more than to tear booster packs on release day and beyond. 

Collector's Guide to Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek

I'll be honest here, there's quite a lot going on with Star Trek. I don't think I've ever looked at a set with so many distinct treatments to collect in both Play and Collector Boosters, which means it's going to be tricky to figure out what players can open where. Fear not, as I'll be doing my best to navigate you through the deep space of collectibility with Star Trek's impending release.

The Autograph Headliners of Star Trek

The Star Trek set does something very different and is very much a first for Magic, and that's autographed cards. It's a no-brainer for a franchise like Star Trek with so many legendary actors, not to mention the interest from collectors in owning cards of their favorite characters. There's seven of these cards to collect:

  • Captain Kathryn Janeway
  • Captain James T. Kirk
  • Lt. Cmdr. Geordi La Forge
  • Mr. Spock, Science Officer
  • Seven of Nine, Unassimilated
  • Captain Jean-Luc Picard
  • Lieutenant Commander Data

These autographed cards only appear in Collector Boosters at extremely low pull rates, and there's 250 of each card available. The cards will always appear in English regardless of the Collector Booster language, and were physically signed by the actors before being added randomly to boosters. These will be some of the most expensive cards to open from Star Trek, although it's unclear what the price will settle at due to other factors such as actor notoriety. 

The Star Trek LCARS Shock Lands (And Where You Can Open Them) 

The Shock Lands make a stunning return in Star Trek, with all ten available to collect on release day on beyond. In particular, the LCARS Shock Lands will be desirable with players and Star Trek collectors, as these give a full-art feel to some of the game's most-played mana options. You can open these in:

Play Boosters:

  • Non-foil LCARS Shock Land card appears less than 1% of the time
  • Non-foil LCARS Shock Land card appears less than 1% of the time
    • Can also appear in the Wildcard slot, also appearing less than 1% of the time

Collector Boosters:

  • Non-foil LCARS Shock Land card appears around 7% of the time
  • Traditional foil LCARS Shock Land card appears nearly 9% of the time
  • Surge foil LCARS Shock Land card appears around 4.5% of the time

These LCARS Shock Lands appear in both Play and Collector Boosters, with the rare opportunity to open these in surge foil only in Collector Boosters. Even if you aren't a big fan of the franchise, this is one of the few collectible treatments that don't immediately scream Star Trek, which means there will be interest in owning these from enfranchised Magic players as well. They seem more common to open in Collector Boosters rather than Play Boosters, but normal printings should be fairly common to open in both. Either way, this means a more affordable route to owning some potent mana options for casual and competitive play. 

The Star Trek Schematics Promo Cards 

The Schematics cards are some of the more striking options from Star Trek, appearing on eight Spacecraft cards from the set. If you're curious what they are, here's the breakdown: 

  • U.S.S. Enterprise-A, Free Spirit
  • H.M.S. Bounty, Unlikely Timeship
  • U.S.S. Reliant, From Hell's Heart
  • D-7 Battle Cruiser
  • U.S.S. Discovery, at Black Alert
  • Borg Cube
  • Deep Space 9
  • U.S.S. Enterprise-D, Galaxy-Class

Unfortunately, these do not appear in Star Trek Play or Collector Boosters. However, they are exclusive to the Beam Me Up Bundle releasing on November 13, 2026. In each Beam Me Up Bundle, there will be two of these Schematics promo cards in traditional foil to collect. This is a similar approach to Reality Fracture's Secret Lair Bundle, which saw ten cards from the set re-imagined with unique Secret Lair art. 

The Star Trek Stardates Cards

The Stardates cards are the bonus sheet for Star Trek, and happen to be reprints of existing Magic cards. There's 30 of these Stardates cards to collect and only appear at mythic rare, with many of these being desirable reprints for enfranchised Magic players to consider picking up. While not everyone will resonate with the aesthetic (such as Benedict Cumberbatch appearing on a reprint of Sheoldred, the Apocalypse), it may present a nice opportunity to snap up on some cards if you can get past the visuals. You can open Stardates cards in:

Play Boosters:

  • Non-foil Stardates cards will appear in roughly 1 out of 25 Play Boosters, and will always replace a common.

Collector Boosters:

  • Non-foil Stardates will appear 23% of the time
  • Traditional foil Stardates cards will appear around 5% of the time

These seem to be more common than the Special Guests that accommodate most in-Magic set releases these days, as the Stardates cards appear in 1 out of 25 Play Boosters. Special Guests is usually 1 in 55, meaning there should be a good amount of circulation and will help with secondary market prices. Traditional foils are exclusive to Collector Boosters and appear in lower quantities. 

The Star Trek Borderless Scene Cards

Borderless cards are a mainstay with every Magic release these days, and they make an exciting return in Star Trek. There's a ton of scene cards encompassing both the Star Trek main set and the Commander subset, you can open these in:

Play Boosters:

  • Uncommon non-foil scene card will appear around 7% of the time
  • Rare non-foil scene card will appear around 1% of the time
  • Mythic rare non-foil scene card will appear around 1% of the time
  • Uncommon traditional foil scene card will appear around 1.5% of the time
  • Rare traditional foil scene cards will appear around 1% of the time
  • Mythic rare traditional foil scene card will appear around 1% of the time
    • A scene card can also appear in the Wildcard slot of a Play Booster at around 1% for each rarity

Collector Boosters:

  • Rare non-foil scene card will appear around 4% of the time
  • Rare non-foil scene card from the Commander: Star Trek subset will appear around 4.5% of the time
  • Mythic rare non-foil scene card will appear around 1.5% of the time
  • Uncommon traditional foil scene card will appear around 27% of the time
  • Rare traditional foil scene card will appear around 5% of the time
  • Mythic rare traditional foil scene card will appear around 2% of the time

In total, there are four of these scenes to collect through opening Play and Collector Boosters. In total, there are 10 uncommon, 8 rare, and 7 mythic rare scene cards that are under the Star Trek main set code. There's a few more under the Commander: Star Trek set code in Collector Boosters, but these are also part of the two Enterprise-Q and Divergent Timelines that you can buy separately.

The Star Trek Borderless Land and Commander Cards

Star Trek also introduces borderless land and borderless commander cards to the mix, and you can open these in:

Play Boosters:

  • Rare non-foil borderless land card will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Mythic rare non-foil borderless land card will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Rare traditional foil borderless land card will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Mythic rare traditional foil borderless land card will appear less than 1% of the time

Collector Boosters:

  • Rare non-foil borderless land card will appear around 3% of the time
  • Mythic rare non-foil borderless land card will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Mythic rare non-foil borderless new-to-Magic commander card will appear around 1% of the time

Borderless commander cards are exclusive to Collector Boosters, and these will either be the face commanders from the preconstructed decks or a couple of other new-to-Magic cards exclusive to these decks. There's ten of the latter to collect, and both appear in traditional foil and non-foil. 

The Showcase Classic Enterprise and LCARS Cards

There's quite a few different showcase treatments in Star Trek with classic Enterprise and the aforementioned LCARS cards. Let's begin with the classic Enterprise cards which can appear in non-foil, traditional foil, and surge foil:

Play Boosters:

  • Uncommon non-foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 4% of the time
  • Rare non-foil classic Enterprise card will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Mythic rare non-foil classic Enterprise card will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Rare traditional foil classic Enterprise card will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Mythic rare traditional foil classic Enterprise card will appear less than 1% of the time

Collector Boosters:

  • Mythic rare non-foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 8% of the time
  • Rare traditional foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 2% of the time
  • Uncommon traditional foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 13% of the time
  • Rare traditional foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 10% of the time
  • Mythic rare traditional foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 2.5% of the time
  • Uncommon surge foil foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 5% of the time
  • Rare surge foil foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 3% of the time
  • Mythic rare surge foil foil classic Enterprise card will appear around 1% of the time

This is unsurprising if you're familiar with the collectibility of Magic, but surge foil copies of this treatment are exclusive to Collector Boosters. There's five uncommon, six mythic rares, and 13 rares of this showcase frame to collect and are available in both Play and Collector Boosters. This is one of the better treatments in my opinion and does a nice job of highlighting the retro feel of Star Trek.

Then there's also the LCARS cards, which also appear on a bunch of non-Shock Land cards in Star Trek. You can find these in:

Play Boosters:

  • Uncommon non-foil LCARS card will appear around 4% of the time
  • Can also appear in the Wildcard slot at any rarity and appear less than 1% of the time
  • Uncommon non-foil LCARS card will appear around 4% of the time
  • Rare non-foil LCARS card will appear around 2% of the time
  • Mythic Rare non-foil LCARS card will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Uncommon, rare, and mythic rare traditional foil LCARS card will appear less than 1% of the time

Collector Boosters:

  • Rare non-foil LCARS card will appear around 10% of the time
  • Mythic Rare non-foil LCARS card will appear around 2% of the time
  • Uncommon traditional foil LCARS card will appear around 19% of the time
  • Rare traditional foil LCARS card will appear around 12% of the time
  • Mythic rare traditional foil LCARS card will appear around 3% of the time
  • Uncommon surge foil LCARS card will appear around 7% of the time
  • Rare surge foil LCARS card will appear around 3% of the time
  • Mythic rare surge foil LCARS card will appear around 1% of the time

The LCARS treatment also appears in surge foil as mentioned with the Shock Lands earlier, and I suspect these will be popular with Star Trek collectors. It compliments the theme of Star Trek well, while also feeling like it's from the original TCG.

The Star Trek Klingon Frame And Klingon Script Cards

We rarely see a completely fictional language printed on Magic cards these days, but Star Trek sees the Klingon language on a select number of cards with a striking Klingon frame treatment to boot. These cards can also appear in English, and the breakdown is:

  • Play Boosters:
    • Common non-foil Klingon frame card will appear around 3% of the time
    • Uncommon non-foil Klingon frame card will appear around 5% of the time
      • Can also appear in the Wildcard slot at any rarity and appear less than 1% of the time
    • Rare non-foil Klingon frame card will appear less than 1% of the time
    • Common, uncommon, or rare traditional foil Klingon frame will appear less than 1% of the time
  • Collector Boosters:
    • Common traditional foil Klingon frame card will appear around 16% of the time
    • Common traditional foil Klingon script card will appear around 8% of the time
    • Rare non-foil Klingon frame card will appear around 2% of the time
    • Rare traditional foil Klingon frame card will appear around 2% of the time
    • Rare traditional foil Klingon script card will appear nearly 3% of the time

It's worth mentioning that the Klingon frame cards only appear in Klingon in Collector Boosters, and will always be in English in Play Boosters. There's one common, six uncommons, and three are Klingon cards to collect — that isn't a lot, so it shouldn't be too hard to collect the set if you're keen to own them all.

The Star Trek Extended-Art Cards 

Lastly, extended-art cards make a return in Star Trek. These are a regular treatment and appear in most Magic sets these days, only appearing on the rares and mythic rares from the set. You can open these in:

Collector Boosters:

  • Rare rare non-foil extended-art card from the Commander: Star Trek subset will appear 93% of the time
  • Rare non-foil extended-art card from the Star Trek main set will appear around 21% of the time
  • Mythic rare non-foil extended-art card from the Star Trek main set will appear around 3% of the time
  • Rare traditional foil extended-art card from the Star Trek main set will appear around 25% of the time
  • Mythic rare traditional foil extended-art card from the Star Trek main set will appear around 3.5% of the time

Extended-art cards only appearing in Collector Boosters is pretty normal for Magic, but it does mean you can open some of the nicer treatments of popular rares and mythic rares. Traditional foil copies add to the value multiplier, and will be of interest to casual Commander players.
